structure: Use one positively associated Gaussian-copula law, separately within each sex/age cell. The source marginals do not determine a joint distribution, so the dependence parameter is an explicit scientific assumption rather than a recovered result. A latent correlation of 0.85 represents strong but imperfect bilateral association without forcing equal ranks or a fixed difference. The supplied arrays are already person-level hand means; no additional trial noise is added. No handedness mixture is introduced because anatomical-side marginals and overall handedness prevalence do not identify handedness-specific joint distributions.

parameter_provenance.parameter: Marginal means and SDs, in kg
parameter_provenance.provenance: Supplied Massy-Westropp table: M50 right 45/8.4 and left 43/8.3; M60 right 40/8.3 and left 38/8; F50 right 28/6.3 and left 26/5.7; F60 right 24/5.3 and left 23/5. Values are rounded mean/SD summaries.
Normality was described by the source, and the supplied grids approximate matching normal quantiles. Pairing uses ranks and preserves the grids rather than fitting new marginals.

parameter_provenance.parameter: Gaussian copula and latent Pearson correlation 0.85 in all four cells
parameter_provenance.provenance: Author-selected working assumptions. Neither study supplies an applicable within-cell inter-hand correlation. Equality of dependence across cells is also assumed.

parameter_provenance.parameter: German individual nondominant/dominant ratio mean 0.9534 and SD 0.11
parameter_provenance.provenance: External contextual evidence only; not used as a correlation, as a ratio of marginal means, or as a quantitative calibration target. Transporting these ratio moments would require additional assumptions about instrument error, anatomical versus dominance labels, and pooling across age and sex.
Specified by the requested virtual study, not estimated from source sample counts. The conflicting reported analytic counts are not used.

requested_estimands.name: Mean absolute anatomical right-left difference, kg
requested_estimands.interpretation: Depends on the assumed copula. Under ideal normal marginals, each cell's signed difference is normal with mean mu_R-mu_L and variance sd_R^2+sd_L^2-2*rho*sd_R*sd_L.

requested_estimands.name: Percentage differing by at least 5 kg
requested_estimands.interpretation: A dependence-sensitive model prediction, not a reported source rate. With ideal normal marginals it is obtained from both tails of the cell-specific signed-difference distribution, then averaged equally over cells.

requested_estimands.name: Mean of both hands, kg
requested_estimands.interpretation: Exactly invariant to the pairing for fixed marginal arrays. The supplied rounded population means imply 33.375 kg under equal cell weights; the actual grid-based result follows the supplied grid means.

requested_estimands.name: Average within-cell rank correlation
requested_estimands.definition: Compute Spearman correlation between paired right and left strengths separately in each cell, using average ranks for ties, then take the unweighted mean of the four correlations.
requested_estimands.interpretation: For continuous population Gaussian copulas, each cell has Spearman correlation (6/pi)*asin(rho/2), approximately 0.838 at rho=0.85. This is not the latent Pearson parameter and is not a pooled correlation. Finite grids and random permutations produce departures; degenerate cells have undefined correlations.

limitations: The first study identifies marginal summaries, not individual pairing, within-cell correlation, absolute-difference distributions, or threshold rates. Many incompatible joint laws share these marginals.
The chosen dependence strength and Gaussian dependence shape are not empirically validated here. Conditional model outputs must not be presented as uniquely evidence-determined estimates.
The German ratio moments do not identify the target kg-scale joint distribution. They describe another instrument, dominance labeling, recruitment restriction, and pooled population.

Applicability is closest to community adults measured with a comparable protocol and exclusions. Recruitment including upper-limb symptoms, arthritis, clinical referrals, occupational selection, or substantially different handedness composition may change both marginals and dependence; transport is not established.
Equal representation is a study-design standardization, not the demographic composition of Northwest Adelaide or another community.
Rounded normal summaries omit tail details and may allow implausible extreme strengths. The generator deliberately preserves supplied values rather than silently truncating them.
Finite-grid rank matching fixes both empirical marginals and introduces permutation constraints; it is not an unconstrained iid sample of bivariate-normal observations.

Proposed validation, not executed: run multiple seeds and grid sizes; verify every block is a permutation; compare simulated estimands with Gaussian population formulas and check finite-grid convergence. Alternative dependence assumptions would require a separate sensitivity analysis rather than being treated as identified alternatives within this primary law.
checks_actually_performed: Arithmetic check using the eight supplied means: their sum is 267 kg, yielding an equal-cell bilateral mean of 267/8 = 33.375 kg.
Mathematical check: assigning left_index[argsort(left_scores)] = 0,...,m-1 creates a local permutation and preserves the entire left marginal in every block.
Code inspection: row identifiers traverse cells in the specified order and ascending supplied right-hand order; the returned frame has only row_id and left_index, both explicitly integer-valued.
Code inspection: randomness is drawn only from the seed-initialized NumPy generator; no external retrieval, SciPy dependency, target fitting, or evaluator feedback is used.
No Python execution, empirical simulation checks, or numerical calibration was performed.
